title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court and the All-China Women's Federation on Further Strengthening Cooperation to Establish and Improve the Work Mechanism for the Protection of the Rights and Interests of Women and Children
full_text_en:
Notice of the Supreme People's Court and the All-China Women's Federation on Further Strengthening Cooperation to Establish and Improve the Working Mechanism for the Protection of Women and Children's Rights and Interests

Fa Fa [2019] No. 21

To: Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; Women's Federations of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Women's Federation of Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

In order to thoroughly implement and promote the Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Further Deepening the Reform of Family Trial Methods and Working Mechanisms (Trial) (Fa Fa [2018] No. 12) and the Opinions of the All-China Women's Federation, the Central Comprehensive Social Management Office, the Supreme People's Court, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of Civil Affairs, and the Ministry of Justice on Preventing and Resolving Marriage and Family Disputes (Fu Zi [2017] No. 13), during the process of deepening the reform of family trials, to strengthen coordination and cooperation between people's courts and women's federation organizations, and to legally protect the legitimate rights and interests of women and children, the following measures are hereby proposed. All localities shall implement them based on actual circumstances.

1. People's courts and women's federation organizations at all levels shall aim to legally protect the legitimate rights and interests of women and children, maintain equal, harmonious, and civilized marriage and family relations, and promote healthy social development. They shall fully exercise their respective functions, strengthen communication, coordination, and cooperation in areas such as family mediation, family investigation, psychological counseling, and anti-domestic violence, and establish and improve a working mechanism for effective connection between court litigation and mediation by women's federation organizations, so as to promote the timely resolution of marriage and family disputes and the effective protection of the legitimate rights and interests of women and children.

2. People's courts at all levels shall establish and improve a working mechanism for communication and coordination with women's federation organizations at the same level. Through means such as holding regular joint work meetings, they shall report on the work of protecting women and children's rights and interests, study and resolve new situations and problems arising in the work, and formulate selection and training plans for personnel such as judges of marriage and family disputes, people's assessors, people's mediators from women's federations, and social investigators.

3. People's courts and women's federation organizations at all levels shall further strengthen cooperation in the field of family mediation. County (city, district) women's federation organizations shall increase their efforts, work together with judicial administrative organs to establish and improve people's mediation committees for marriage and family disputes, select and appoint full-time people's mediators, strengthen the work of professionals in the fields of law, psychology, social work, and women's federation rights protection serving as people's mediators, and deeply carry out mediation of marriage and family disputes. People's courts encourage and support the participation of women's federation organizations in the court's litigation and mediation connection work. When people's courts cooperate with women's federation organizations in special invited mediation, they shall include people's mediation committees for marriage and family disputes and people's mediators in the court's roster of special invited mediation organizations and special invited mediators.

For cases referred, entrusted, or assigned for special invited mediation by people's courts, people's mediation committees for marriage and family disputes and people's mediators may, within their scope of authority, fully utilize the professional advantages and traditional experience of women's federation organizations in carrying out family work, and conscientiously organize and carry out mediation work. Women's federation organizations and people's mediators shall maintain contact with the people's court regarding the progress of the case and promptly inform the court of the mediation result.

4. People's courts and women's federation organizations at all levels shall further strengthen cooperation in the field of entrusted family investigation. Women's federation organizations at all levels shall actively recommend to people's courts at the same level personnel who have gender awareness and are familiar with professional knowledge in areas such as law, psychology, and marriage and family as candidates for family investigators. People's courts shall establish and improve a roster of family investigators, and make normative provisions and requirements for the conduct of family investigations and the preparation of investigation reports, which family investigators shall follow. If a party to the case raises objections to the content of the investigation report, the people's court may require the family investigator to appear in court to explain the situation, or the family investigator may provide a written explanation of the party's objections.

5. For litigation involving parental rights such as divorce, child support, custody, and visitation rights concerning minors, people's courts and women's federation organizations shall strengthen cooperation on parental education for parents. During litigation, people's courts shall provide litigation guidance to parents, guiding them to consider parental rights litigation from the perspective of the best interests of the child and to resolve family conflicts. People's courts may also entrust women's federation organizations to recommend professional resources to carry out parental education for parents, actively guiding parents to correctly handle parent-child relationships and family conflicts.

6. In the selection and appointment of people's assessors, women's federation organizations and people's courts at all levels shall further strengthen communication and cooperation. In cases involving marriage and family disputes, people's courts may request local women's federation organizations to recommend personnel who meet basic conditions, have awareness of gender equality and the best interests of children, are familiar with the psychological characteristics of women and children, and are good at conducting ideological work as candidates for people's assessors, thereby fully leveraging the advantages of people's assessors from women's federations.

7. When hearing family dispute cases, people's courts may, based on the needs of the case, entrust professional psychological counseling institutions recommended by women's federation organizations to provide services related to mental health, such as marriage psychological counseling, analysis of family conflicts, and scientific parenting guidance, to help family members involved in the case relieve psychological stress and negative emotions, and provide psychological support for the proper handling of family disputes.

8. People's courts may request family investigators, people's assessors, and people's mediators to participate in social observation and protection after the conclusion of the case, or may, based on the needs of the case, entrust women's federation organizations to recommend relevant personnel to conduct follow-up visits and observation of the living conditions and post-dispute situation of the parties involved, especially women and child parties with domestic violence factors, and provide feedback to the people's court on the results of such visits and observation.

9. People's courts at all levels shall establish and improve an interactive mechanism for petition letters and visits with women's federation organizations. Women's federation organizations may communicate in a timely manner with the petition department of the people's court regarding petition letters and visits involving litigation where they need to understand the case situation. The petition department of the people's court may also, regarding petition letters and visits involving the protection of women and children's rights and interests, invite women's federation organizations to jointly participate in conflict resolution.

10. Women's federation organizations and people's courts at all levels shall jointly carry out publicity and education activities on the basic state policy of gender equality, the Marriage Law, the Anti-Domestic Violence Law, the Law on the Protection of Women's Rights and Interests, and the Law on the Protection of Minors, with emphasis on the promotion of socialist core values. They shall innovate in the carriers and positions of publicity and education, strengthen the use of new media technology in publicity and education, and carry out publicity and education activities through diversified forms such as micro-videos, micro-interviews, and micro-cases, so as to create a good legal atmosphere.

11. People's courts and women's federation organizations at all levels shall establish and improve a cooperative training mechanism and increase the intensity of two-way exchange training. Through methods such as regular training and explaining the law through cases, people's courts and women's federation organizations shall strengthen training in legal business, mental health, gender equality, and the awareness of the best interests of children, which are closely related to the protection of women and children's rights and interests, for personnel such as family case judges, people's mediators for marriage and family disputes, people's assessors, family investigators, and social observers, so as to enhance their ability to prevent and handle marriage and family disputes.

12. When hearing family dispute cases, people's courts at all levels shall pay attention to citing relevant provisions of the Law on the Protection of Women's Rights and Interests, the Law on the Protection of Minors, the Anti-Domestic Violence Law, and other related laws, so as to truly implement the legislative spirit of protecting women and children's rights in judicial practice. In the reasoning part of the judgment, attention shall be paid to reflecting the integration of reason, emotion, and law, and to promoting socialist core values.

13. People's courts and women's federation organizations at all levels shall focus on key and difficult issues in the field of marriage and family, such as the protection of minors and anti-domestic violence, further strengthen cooperation, and through means such as regular joint meetings, communicate and summarize in a timely manner, propose countermeasures, form research reports, and promote the improvement of laws, regulations, and public policies closely related to the interests of women and children. People's courts at all levels shall conscientiously summarize the experience of reforming family trial methods and working mechanisms, further innovate trial practices in aspects such as family litigation procedures and assessment and evaluation, and form research results.

14. For lawsuits involving serious infringement of women and children's rights and interests, such as tort actions or personal safety protection orders, people's courts at all levels shall open or improve 'green channels' to hear cases swiftly and quickly, and promptly protect the legitimate rights and interests of women and children. They shall further unify the standards for determining the facts of domestic violence, increase the intensity of ex officio evidence collection, and appropriately reduce the burden of proof on the injured party. When women's federation organizations at all levels receive complaints, reports, or requests for help regarding domestic violence, they shall promptly provide assistance to the victims of domestic violence, conduct legal education on the perpetrators, and when necessary, may introduce professional resources to provide psychological counseling to both the perpetrator and the victim. If a party is a person without or with limited capacity for civil conduct, or is unable to apply for a personal safety protection order on their own due to coercion or intimidation, the women's federation organization, upon receiving a request for help, may apply to the people's court on behalf of the party.

August 16, 2019
